summary: Aermotor observation cab on an 80-foot steel tower in the Eldorado National Forest; built 1937, now closed, with a 2004 register note that dismantling was planned.

facts.design: Aermotor 7x7 observation cab on an 80-foot X-brace open steel tower, with a BC-201 cabin for the operator

access.note: Register note says the lookout is closed; the grounds are accessible to visitors

visit.trail_note: Closed lookout; visitors should not climb it. The June 2020 visit report says the tower is in rough shape, with the first two flights of stairs missing and all of the glass broken out.

events.note: Annual forest fire guard school opened at Armstrong Lookout the week before the June 2, 1938 Mountain Democrat notice; Ranger George B. Young of Lumberyard District in charge
January 1, 2003 register comment recalls a lookout named Mike moving to the hill in 1939 or 1940
Same recollection says Mike stayed until about 1943

September 4, 2004 register comment: lookout closed, grounds accessible; a USFS employee said it is scheduled for dismantling, but the Eldorado NF has no money for that at this time; four structures on site
June 12, 2020 visit report: tower in rough shape; first two flights of stairs missing; glass broken out

notes_for_editor: Two sources only: the NHLR entry (a 1939-43 recollection in a January 2003 visit comment, a September 2004 comment on closure and dismantling, and a June 2020 visit report) and one June 1938 Mountain Democrat item quoted on Forest Lookouts. The 1937 build year is the register's; the 1938 item shows the site in use by then but does not date construction. The 1939 and 1943 staffing dates come from the recollection and are approximate. The lineman's-steps tree is reported as the writer's memory and appears in the story only as that memory. Current closure and dismantling status were not checked; two web searches found nothing further. Record height was blank and is filled from the register (80 ft = 24.4 m). Staffing as_of is now the 2020 visit report, not undated.
